extracted.intended_audience: prospective artists applying for a MacDowell Fellowship / artist residency applicants
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and requirements for artists applying to the MacDowell artist residency fellowship, including what selection panels consider, eligibility by discipline, application deadlines, and logistical/financial information. Intended to help applicants prepare and submit a competitive application for a specific institutional residency program.

rubrics_metrics.name: Artistic excellence (sole criterion for acceptance)
rubrics_metrics.description: About 300 artists in seven disciplines are awarded Fellowships each year and the sole criterion for acceptance is artistic excellence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The program emphasizes artistic excellence above all. The page notes a very competitive applicant pool and limited number of studios, so artistic excellence is assessed relative to many talented applicants. Applicants should present their strongest demonstration of artistic quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Professional achievements / prior body of work
rubrics_metrics.description: A list of professional achievements in an artistic field (consideration of your prior body of work).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection panels consider your prior accomplishments as evidence of sustained practice and achievement. Prepare a clear, organized list of professional milestones and past work to demonstrate your artistic track record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Current work sample (demonstration of your practice)
rubrics_metrics.description: A current work sample (demonstration of your practice).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work samples are a primary element of evaluation; applicants should follow the linked 'Work Sample Requirements' for format and content. The sample should represent current practice and be chosen to best illustrate artistic quality and capability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project proposal (what you hope to accomplish with your residency)
rubrics_metrics.description: Your project proposal (what you hope to accomplish with your residency).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The proposal should clearly state goals for the residency and how you intend to use the time/studio to advance your work. Selection panels weigh the proposed plan alongside the applicant's practice and work samples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discipline eligibility / fit
rubrics_metrics.description: MacDowell encourages applications from artists of all backgrounds and all countries in the following disciplines: architecture, film/video, interdisciplinary arts, literature, music composition, theatre, and visual arts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should apply within one of the listed disciplines. If a proposed project does not fall clearly within one of these artistic disciplines, applicants are advised to contact the admissions department for guidance. Discipline fit informs panel assignment and evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant status: established and emerging artists eligible
rubrics_metrics.description: Artists established as well as artists in development are eligible to complete the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Both emerging and established artists may apply; panels evaluate quality and potential rather than career stage alone. Emphasize strengths appropriate to your career stage in achievements, samples, and proposal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intentionality / preparedness for residency
rubrics_metrics.description: Those who arrive for a residency with intentionality, frequently enter a period of intense productivity and in many cases have a transformative experience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants who convey a clear plan and readiness to use residency time productively are implied to be stronger candidates. Demonstrate preparedness and concrete objectives in the project proposal and supporting materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application timing, deadlines, and residency windows
rubrics_metrics.description: Application deadlines and residency windows are required: e.g., Spring/Summer 2027 residencies (March 1–August 31, 2027) — Applications open Aug 15, 2026; Application deadline Sep 10, 2026. Fall/Winter 2027–2028 residencies (Sept 1, 2027–Feb 29, 2028) — Applications open Jan 15, 2027; Application deadline Feb 10, 2027.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must apply within posted application windows and select residency dates that align with the residency periods. Late or out-of-window submissions will not meet procedural requirements. Refer to the page for specific cycle dates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language recommendation / accessibility
rubrics_metrics.description: It is recommended to have conversational English, as MacDowell does not provide interpreter services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-native English speakers are encouraged to have conversational English to participate fully in residency activities. Applicants who require interpretation should contact admissions to discuss accommodations, but the page cautions that interpretation services are not provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fees and financial assistance
rubrics_metrics.description: There are no residency fees, and need-based stipends and travel reimbursement grants are available to open the residency to the broadest possible community of artists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants may apply for need-based financial assistance and travel reimbursement; the residency itself has no fee. Include any requested financial-aid documentation as directed by the application process. Financial assistance is intended to broaden accessibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capacity constraint (number of studios limits offers)
rubrics_metrics.description: While the program would like to offer more Fellowships, it is limited by the number of studios available on campus.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection is influenced by institutional capacity; even highly qualified applicants may not receive offers due to limited studio availability. This operational constraint contributes to competitiveness and should be considered when planning application timing and flexibility in residency dates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Where to find additional application guidance (linked resources)
rubrics_metrics.description: Additional Resources: How to Apply video; Application Guidelines; Disciplines; Work Sample Requirements; Financial Assistance; What to Expect in Peterborough; FAQs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should consult the linked resources for detailed instructions, formatting rules, sample requirements, and FAQs. Specifics (e.g., work sample formats, file types, length limits) are provided in those resources rather than on the main page.
